item.title: Listen: What happened with the Ukraine-Russia peace negociations?
item.description: Peace talks between Ukraine and Russia are constantly being delayed. That’s what Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky stated last week. As his country begins to run out of missiles and financial support, can Zelensky still hope to get out of this war with dignity?

item.title: How Iran war exposes Europe’s dangerous dependency on fertilisers
item.description: Roughly a third of the world’s fertiliser exports pass through the Strait of Hormuz, a narrow chokepoint now blocked by Iran in response to being attacked. Within days of the latest escalation, fertiliser prices surged, with urea (a nitrogen-based fertiliser) jumping sharply across global markets.

item.title: The new ‘Brussels effect’ — learning to be silent on US-Israel to keep funding
item.description: Debates are becoming more muted as equality experts and activists learn to be silent on questions like Gaza and the illegal US and Israeli attack on Iran for fear of losing their access to much-needed EU funding. It is, as one conference participant says wryly: “The new Brussels effect”.

item.title: EU and Australia agree pact to boost trade and security, after eight-year negotiations
item.description: The deal grants Australia quota-based access for beef, lamb, and dairy products to the EU, while European exporters gain near-zero tariffs on vehicles, dairy, and other goods.

item.title: How Orbán could still rule even if Tisza wins: five scenarios for the Hungarian election
item.description: Viktor Orbán's Fidesz needs fewer votes than the opposition Tisza party to stay in power, as the electoral system still favours the incumbent. In this article, we examine the most likely developments after the Hungarian elections on 12 April.

item.title: Kremlin-hated Hungarian killing 400 Russian soldiers to 1 (Ukraine Battlefield update, day 1,489)
item.description: The cost of "eliminating" a Russian soldier was €758, said Magyar: "We should be exchanging plastic and metal for dead Russians. It is the best exchange rate".

item.title: Japan’s election win is a warning for Europe’s comfort zone
item.description: Europe should recognise that Japan has already confronted dilemmas we are only now fully acknowledging: how to stay open without becoming exposed, and how to deepen security ties without trading away a rules-based identity.

item.title: Kallas takes aim at Russia’s ‘unethical’ army recruiting in Africa during Ghana trip
item.description: A report by the All Eyes on Wagner investigative group listed 1,417 fighters from 35 African countries who had joined the Russian army between 2023 and mid-2025, 316 of whom have been killed. Ghana’s West African neighbour Cameroon has suffered the highest losses: 94 of its 335 recruits have been killed during Russia’s war in Ukraine.

item.title: EU postpones Russian oil-ban, as Iran energy shock aggravates rifts
item.description: Russian oil deliveries to Hungary jumped from 61 percent of its imports in 2021 to 93 percent in 2025 despite the Ukraine war.

item.title: European universities ‘complicit in border violence and rights abuses’, report finds
item.description: Universities play a significant, if often obscured, role in the development, perpetuation and expansion of Fortress Europe, says the Transnational Institute report.

item.title: Now Babiš’ Czech Republic wants a Russian-style ‘foreign agents’ law against NGOs
item.description: The initiative aims to give the government power to arbitrarily persecute anyone, including universities, activists, media, NGOs and others. Those who opt not to register would face fines of up to €600,000.

item.title: Trump’s military options to secure Hormuz and end the war, explained
item.description: As Qatar’s gas stops flowing to Europe and Iran chokes the Strait of Hormuz, energy prices are surging and tensions have spiked. US threats raise the stakes — but reopening this vital artery is far from simple, with risky military options, asymmetric warfare, and the looming threat of mined waters hanging over global trade. Here are some basic questions and answers.

item.title: Listen: Is Italy’s Giorgia Meloni losing her grip on power after a failed referendum?
item.description: Is Giorgia Meloni’s grip on power slipping? After a stinging referendum defeat over judicial reforms, the Italian PM faces her first major domestic setback. Could this first setback weaken her both in Italy and internationally?

item.title: Russian journalists see frontline stalemate: infantry at end of human endurance (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,490)
item.description: "Mechanised armies of the 20th century have lost their meaning and the infantryman has reached the limits of human capability," said one Russian military expert.

item.title: EU single market for services still riddled with barriers after 20 years, critical report finds
item.description: A new report finds Brussels has made little headway in opening up Europe's services markets since the landmark Services Directive came into force in 2006.
